belief: If I forget things, people will think less of me.
origins: Embarrassment about missing names, repeating stories, or losing track of the conversation can lead to avoiding gatherings or hiding the problem.
teaches: “Man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.” “Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.” “The parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable.” True friends value you more than your memory. Being honest about your difficulty often brings understanding and help, and makes it easier to enjoy company. God never forgets you: “I have inscribed you on the palms of My hands.”
self_statements: They will think I am senile.
errors: Believing people either respect me or think less of me.
Feeling embarrassed and concluding I am judged.
questions: What do my close friends say when I forget?
What would I think of a friend who forgot a name?
What could I say to put people at ease?
What tools could help, like name tags, notes, or photos?
What does God say about me?
truth: My value to others and to God does not depend on my memory. I can be honest, use helpful tools, and enjoy people. God has not forgotten me.
hw_truths: God has inscribed me on His hands.
log: Each week, note one gathering you enjoyed.
actions: Try, “My memory is slower now, so please be patient.”
Remember God does not forget you.
prayer: Lord, I forget and I am embarrassed. Thank You that You never forget me. Give me honest friends and ease with others. Amen.
